The near-cutoff error is partitioned into short intervals and bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz using fourth-moment and short-interval second-moment estimates, while far terms use absolute convergence.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Gives the first quantitative bridge from the analytic series to a sharp cutoff.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: High: decomposition logic is prose-supported; exact interval parameters and error exponents require scan verification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: An unweighted signed sum requires a separate short-interval moment estimate
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Removing smoothing cannot rely on positivity of cubic central values, so the proof imports a short-interval second-moment bound obtained from a degree-two corrected double series with nonnegative coefficients.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The functional equation converts the left contour into an oscillatory integral with a square-root saving
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: After contour shifting, a possible reflected-pole residue and three contour integrals appear. Reflecting the left edge into absolute convergence yields gamma-ratio phases; a second-derivative estimate saves a half-power of the height parameter.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The smoothed result follows directly from continuation and vertical growth, whereas the sharp cutoff additionally needs short-interval control, a truncated Perron decomposition, an oscillatory functional-equation saving, and a constrained balance of errors.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The resulting exponent is conditional on the specific mean-value inputs and bounds used here and is not presented as an intrinsic barrier.
